headline: High risk of shared-filesystem prompt injection and data leakage; Cursor can write/egress broadly while gpt-researcher reads and uploads documents by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor can write/read workspace files, use MCP, and shares state via local filesystem; gpt-researcher reads local documents and uses MCP. That creates a plausible default bridge where content from one can be treated as instructions by the other. The pathway is not proven to be fully automatic, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF Cursor writes attacker-controlled text into a shared workspace file that gpt-researcher later ingests
IF either agent parses file contents or MCP outputs as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP on at least one agent for shared tasks
Add a manual review step before gpt-researcher consumes Cursor-generated files
Use read-only mounts for inputs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, clipboard contents, and has broad network egress; gpt-researcher reads local documents and sends queries/reports through external APIs. If sensitive files are shared, Cursor can expose them into the pair and gpt-researcher can transmit them onward, creating a realistic exfiltration path in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive source code or documents are opened in Cursor and then placed in a shared workspace
IF gpt-researcher processes those files and sends derived content to OpenAI/Tavily/LangChain/Gemini APIs
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of the shared workspace
Disable network egress for one agent during sensitive tasks
Use separate API keys and projects per agent
Redact secrets before handing files to gpt-researcher
requires-engineering: enforce DLP or egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can read and write local files, spawn subprocesses, and install packages; Cursor also modifies git state. In a shared directory, concurrent edits and package changes can collide and corrupt state or commits. Because the overlap is broad and default coordination is not documented, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or output directory
IF either agent installs packages or rewrites files while the other is active
mitigations: Run agents in separate clones
Serialize write access with a lock file
Disable package installation for one agent
Pause one agent before git operations
requires-engineering: add workspace-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher is designed to produce research reports and citations, while Cursor can act on files and git state. If Cursor consumes gpt-researcher output without verification, mistaken or hallucinated research can cascade into code or documentation changes. The action path exists, but it is not inherently automatic.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher output is copied into Cursor as authoritative input
IF Cursor uses that output to edit files or commit changes without independent verification
mitigations: Require source-link checks before acting on reports
Have Cursor open the cited sources before edits
Use a second-pass human review for factual claims
Limit gpt-researcher output to drafts only
requires-engineering: add citation validation gates

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor handles clipboard contents and open files, while gpt-researcher processes local documents and sends them to third-party APIs. If regulated or residency-bound data is placed in the shared workflow, the pair can create retention and transfer mismatches. The profiles do not specify certifications, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than higher.
conditions: IF EU PII, PHI, or other regulated data is opened in Cursor and then passed to gpt-researcher
IF the external APIs used by gpt-researcher are not covered by the required DPA or residency terms
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared tasks
Confirm vendor DPAs before use
Strip identifiers before research runs
Keep audit logs of data handoff
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
